E045: +0.18 pp, below the +0.2 bar and within the ~0.13 pp paired sd. E049: x3 matched x2 (-0.03). x2 was force-kept, but the gain is not established.
E042 jitter: +0.16 pp, re-draw-sized. Removing translate (H1.8.2) and stage-coupled augmentation (D017) are untested.
E042: +0.16 pp at +0.5% time. That is below the +0.2 bar and within noise. Force-kept.

Search: Hiverge's 0.50->0.08 magnitude schedule was co-tuned with no lookahead, no warmup and Muon lr 0.205. A lower target also acts as a lower Muon lr, which has never been tested (review). Run the lr 0.11 control (H1.2 child) first.

updates.statement: With the recipe held fixed, per-step GPU work can still be cut by a few percent at unchanged accuracy. The cut must remove GPU work, not launches; launch overhead is hidden (E005, E038). Systems keeps total ~11% (E007 ~1%, E010 2.0%, E021 2.2%, E023 2.7%, E034 3.0%). The resolution curriculum (H2.3) has added FLOP cuts: E040 -3.0%, E047 -3.5%, E048 -5.2%. Candidates left: Muon projection frequency (H2.4.3), NS2 with per-iteration (Polar Express) coefficients, re-checking max-autotune (H2.5.1), and trial-0 warmup gaps (H3.2). Conv-shape levers are <=~1% (E032).
updates.reason: Updated with the curriculum keeps and the search findings (Turbo-Muon weakens AOL-NS2; Polar Express is the better route).

updates.statement: Progressive resizing as a curriculum of bilinearly downsampled whole images (antialiased, inside the compiled augment) cuts FLOPs at almost no accuracy cost, as long as the low-res steps fall in or near warmup. On the bs-1536 Muon base, 20 px for epochs 0-1.5, then 28 px for 1.5-3.0, then 32 px for 3.75 epochs (E048) reaches 0.7552 at 5.00 s. Measured: 24 px warmup stage -3.0% / +0.08 pp (E040); 24->20 px -3.5% / -0.18 pp (E047); 28 px stage -5.2% / +0.02 pp (E048; -0.23 pp in E044). Pushing low-res into the peak-lr phase hurt (E043, -0.38 pp). 16 px collapsed (E050, -1.41 pp; final map 1x1, plus the whitening-bias confound, N1.a). Each resolution needs its own compiled graph and a static-kernel max_pool2d (not amax).
updates.reason: E040+, E047+ and E048+ are the actual evidence for this Lvl2 mechanism (re-filed from H2.3.2/H2.3.3 per the review). E043~ and E050- bound it.

Untested as stated (thirds at 24/28/32 with +15% epochs). E040 ran 1.5 epochs at 24 px and belongs to H2.3. On our cost ratios, the Fable-style longer total with ~2/3 low-res epochs adds time unless the 32 px tail is cut, and that question is now N1.c.1.

updates.statement: On the bs-1536 Muon base, inserting a 1.5-epoch 28 px stage between the low-res warmup stage and 32 px, at unchanged total epochs (6.75) and step-indexed schedules, cuts time by >=3% with mean accuracy within -0.25 pp. (Rewritten to match what was run. The original specified 3 epochs at 28 px and a 7.0-epoch total.)
updates.reason: E044: -4.4% time, -0.23 pp (24 px base). E048: -5.2%, +0.02 pp (20 px base). Both are inside the rewritten bounds. The difference between them is within the paired sd, and offline extra seeds would settle the real marginal cost (new H4.1 child).

Unchanged evidence. Candidate list revised by search: AOL-NS2 is weakened (Turbo-Muon table), Polar Express NS2 and FreezeOut were added as new children, and projection frequency stays the top candidate.

Search confirms that both CIFAR-10 records use norm_freq = 2+int(15p), though neither ablates it. The review ranks it as the next systems run. It changes no math early and compounds with the curriculum.
Turbo-Muon's own table: AOL with 2 iterations (3.32) is worse than plain NS3 (3.30), and its CIFAR speedrun gained only 0.8% going 5->4. Superseded by the Polar Express variant (new child).
Not yet run. The review adds that SXM-tuned kernel choices may not transfer to the PCIe judge, so this also bears on the official score. Run 2-3 interleaved reps.

updates.statement: The binding constraint is the accuracy gate, and the 3-seed mean is optimistically biased for the 40-seed judge. The tip (E048, 0.7552, seed 0 at 0.7527) sits on a ratchet: re-draw-sized gains were force-kept (E024 +0.17, E026 +0.18, E042 +0.16, E045 +0.18) and similar losses discarded (E031, E036, E046, E049). The paired sd of a trajectory-changing edit is ~0.12-0.15 pp; for example, the same 28 px stage scored -0.23 (E044) and +0.02 (E048). So deltas under ~0.3 pp from a single 3-seed run are inconclusive. Measuring the tip on extra seeds decides how much margin is real against 0.75 and how close to the knee further cuts can go.
updates.reason: Review: selection on noise, plus the E044/E048 pair, contradict the <=0.06 pp sd reading. The extra-seed checks have never been run.

updates.statement: A bit-identical commit reruns deterministically in accuracy, with ~1% timing jitter (E003). Edits that preserve the math, or change it only after epoch 1, move the 3-seed mean by <=0.07 pp (E028, E032, E034, E035, E038). Edits that change the trajectory from step 0 move it by 0.10-0.26 pp (E041, E042, E045, E046, E047), and the same 28 px stage gave -0.23 vs +0.02 (E044/E048). Working paired sd for real recipe changes: ~0.12-0.15 pp. Fable's CIFAR-10 per-trial sd of ~0.15 pp (3-seed ~0.09) is a lower bound for CIFAR-100.
updates.reason: Review and search. The earlier <=0.06 pp inference rested on edits that barely change the trajectory.
Never run, and now top priority (review). The force-keep ratchet predicts the extra-seed mean will fall below the seeds 0-2 mean, so 'within 0.15 pp' is less likely than before.
The ratchet argument makes it more likely that the E024/E026 keeps were re-draws. Still unrun.
Post-E040 deltas and the E044/E048 pair point to a paired sd of ~0.12-0.15, not <=0.06. Kept open because the run itself is cheap and decisive.

For resolution, reallocating FLOPs beats epochs by far more than the 0.03 pp per 1% band. E040 cost ~0 pp per 1%, E047 0.05, E044 0.052 and E048 ~0, against ~0.12-0.15 for epochs at the knee. Cumulatively, E034 -> E048 went from 5.89 to 5.00 s at equal accuracy. The narrow width/depth part still holds (E029, E037; see H1.5 and H5.1). The replacement Lvl1 is N1.

new.statement: The score is set by the number of full-resolution steps after warmup. Steps during warmup and early training can be made much cheaper (lower resolution, possibly larger batch) at almost no accuracy cost; E040, E047 and E048 cut 12% of time at equal accuracy. How cheap the early phase can go is limited by structural thresholds, not by image information: the final map must stay >=2x2, and the whitening bias is fitted at low res and then frozen. Low-res steps placed after the lr peak do cost accuracy (E043). The remaining time lies in (a) cheaper early steps, (b) fewer early steps through larger batches, and (c) the length of the 32 px tail.

The 16 px collapse (E050, -1.41 pp) and part of the 20 px cost (E047, -0.18 pp) come from two structural effects. First, at 16 px the final map is 1x1, so global max-pool selection vanishes. Second, the whitening bias trains only in epoch 1, which runs entirely at low resolution; it is fitted to blurred low-res patch statistics and then frozen for the 32 px stages. Which effect dominates is untested.

On the E048 tip, training the whitening bias through the end of the 28 px stage (epoch 3.0) instead of epoch 1, with both graph variants warmed up in build(), raises mean accuracy by >=+0.2 pp at <=1.5% more time. If it does, the bias freeze is what limits how cheap the early phase can be. A change within +-0.1 pp refutes the confound at 20 px.

On the E048 tip, replacing the 20 px first stage with 18 px keeps a 2x2 final map (whitening 17 -> pools 8/4/2). That cuts mean time by >=1% with mean accuracy within -0.25 pp of the tip. A loss of >=0.6 pp would mean the 1x1-map story does not explain E050, which points to N1.a.1.

In the low-res stages, small feature maps are latency-bound (E050 saved little time), and warmup steps tolerate low fidelity (E040, E047). So a larger batch there raises throughput and cuts steps where they matter least. It should not cost the accuracy that a flat bs increase cost (E041, -0.26 pp).

On the E048 tip, use bs 3072 in the 20 px and 28 px stages and keep bs 1536 at 32 px. Index all schedules by samples seen, keep Muon lr and momentum unchanged at the switch, and leave the SGD-group per-sample lr unchanged. Gate it in drafts/ first: skip the run if the per-epoch saving of the low-res stages is <15%. Prediction: mean time falls by >=2.5% with mean accuracy within -0.2 pp. Do not move a resolution boundary in the same run (C0235).
The final 32 px stage acts as a FixRes-style fine-tune. Post-warmup steps need near-full resolution, but 28 px may be close enough to replace part of the 3.75-epoch 32 px tail.

On the E048 tip, extend the 28 px stage from 1.5 to 2.25 epochs and shorten the 32 px stage from 3.75 to 3.0, keeping 6.75 total epochs and the step-indexed schedules. Prediction: mean time falls by >=2.5%, and accuracy stays >=0.753 and within -0.2 pp of the tip. If it loses >=0.35 pp, as E043 did, the post-warmup steps need 32 px and the tail is at its floor.

Muon lr control below the tested range. On the E048 tip, lowering the Muon lr from 0.16 to 0.11, with nothing else changed, moves mean accuracy by no more than +-0.2 pp. This must run before H1.9.1, so that a positive NS-magnitude-schedule result is not just a lower effective lr.

Late batch ramp. On the E048 tip, keep bs 1536 until ~70% of samples seen, then switch to bs 2048 for the rest of the 32 px stage. Index schedules by samples seen, keep Muon lr and momentum unchanged, and warm up all shapes in build(). Prediction: mean time falls by >=2% with accuracy within -0.2 pp. A drop of >=0.25 pp is read as over-annealing (C0209, as in E025); the follow-up is a smaller final batch.

NorMuon. On the E048 tip, add per-row second-moment normalization after NS3 (NorMuon) in the batched compiled Muon step, keeping the weight-norm projection. Prediction: >=+0.25 pp mean accuracy at <=1% more time. Untested on CNN filters.

The 100-way head is the only SGD-group parameter that has proved sensitive (E039). Its update geometry, as opposed to its lr scale, may be limiting: an SGD head update is dominated by a few frequent-gradient directions. Giving it a normalized or orthogonalized update balances the class directions.

On the E048 tip, optimize the [100, 576] head with Muon (NS3, momentum 0.8, lr chosen so the first-step update RMS matches the current SGD head's), removing it from the SGD group. Prediction: >=+0.25 pp mean accuracy at <=1% more time.

Two NS iterations with per-iteration minimax coefficients (Polar Express), tuned for the singular-value range of the tip's momentum matrices, save >=0.2 ms/step of Muon GPU time (drafts/time_muon.py) and >=1% mean time, with accuracy within +-0.2 pp.

FreezeOut-style: freeze block 1 (conv weights and BN biases) for the last ~20% of steps through a compiled graph variant that detaches block 1's output. This skips block 1's wgrad and its Muon work, cutting mean time by >=3% with accuracy within -0.2 pp. Prior is low: there was no gain on VGG-like nets, and E037 showed block-1 capacity matters under Muon.

On the E048 tip (6+ compiled variants), trial 0's train time is within 1% of the mean of trials 1-2, so no warmup gap leaks into the timed region. Check from the per-trial times; if it fails, fix the warmup layout or shape before anything else.

Offline in drafts/ on seeds 3-12, the E048 tip with the 28 px stage and the same commit without it (the E047 config) differ in mean accuracy by <=0.12 pp. That would mean the E044 (-0.23) vs E048 (+0.02) gap was re-draw noise, not an interaction with the 20 px stage or the head lr.

Augmentation strength should rise with resolution. On the E048 tip, turning off brightness/contrast jitter in the 20 px and 28 px stages, and keeping it plus translate-2 at 32 px, gives >=+0.2 pp mean accuracy at unchanged time. Caveat: translate is applied before downsampling, so it is not stronger at low res (D018).

structured_output.summary:
I've brought the tree up to date with the 5.00 s tip (E048) and taken the review's points on board. H1 is rewritten: update structure (Muon and lookahead) still sets accuracy per step, but recent time cuts came from cheaper or fewer steps. Every scalar re-tune since E024 is now classed as re-draw noise. H5 ("no reallocation beats epochs") is refuted for resolution, since E040, E047 and E048 cost ~0-0.05 pp per 1% of time against ~0.12-0.15 for epochs. A new Lvl1, N1, replaces it: post-warmup full-res steps set the score, and how cheap the early phase can be is limited by structural thresholds. Its children cover the whitening-bias-freeze confound vs the 1x1-map explanation (N1.a.1, N1.a.2), a larger batch in the low-res stages (N1.b.1), and the length of the 32 px tail (N1.c.1).

On the curriculum branch, E040, E047 and E048 are re-filed as evidence for H2.3, which is now supported. H2.3.2 is retired as untested-as-stated. H2.3.3 is rewritten to match what was actually run and marked supported.

H4 and H4.1 now carry a working paired sd of ~0.12-0.15 pp, the force-keep ratchet bias and the E044/E048 discrepancy. Confidence in H4.1.4 (sd <=0.06) is lowered. The extra-seed checks (H4.1.2) and the 28 px marginal-cost check (N6) are now priorities.

H1.6.6 is widened to check whether E046 and E049 also changed the weights at all; this cheap check gates several axis closures. H1.2.3 is marked inconclusive, and N1.e (late batch ramp) and N1.f (NorMuon) are added under H1.2. N1.d, a Muon lr 0.11 control, must run before H1.9.1. H2.4.5 (AOL-NS2) is lowered because the Turbo-Muon paper's own results weaken it; Polar Express NS2 (N3) and FreezeOut (N4) are added as alternatives. Other changes:
- H2.4.3 (projection frequency) is the next systems run.
- H1.4 is lowered.
- H1.7.3 and H1.8.1 are inconclusive.
- N2 adds a node for the head's update geometry.
- N5 adds a trial-0 timing check.
- N7 adds augmentation coupled to resolution.

The open Lvl1s are H1, H2, H4 and N1.
